business_model: A monthly subscription per studio workspace for a shared job board.

hires.start: Not paid in the model period

benchmarks.benchmark: Reaches profit on current costs and growth before cash runs out
benchmarks.source: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead?

drivers.value: 1 a month from Month 2, reaching 10 in Month 11
drivers.label: assumption
drivers.basis: Business plan objective of ten studios in the first year.

drivers.label: assumption
drivers.basis: No studio has paid yet, so no churn is measured.

drivers.label: derived
drivers.basis: Hosting 100 + software tools 50. No paid staff.

break_even: Month 5, at 4 studios: 4 × 40 = 160 covers 150 of monthly costs.
runway: Not limited on the base plan. Cash is lowest at 7,640 in Month 4, and the company is profitable from Month 5. At the Month 1 burn of 150, starting cash alone would last about 53 months.

unit_economics.formula: Gross profit 1,400 ÷ revenue 2,600. Rises as studios share the fixed hosting cost.
Not measured. The base model assumes no cancellations.
Paid spend is 0. Founder time is the only cost.

default_alive_reason: There is no revenue history yet, so no real growth rate can be read. If the ramp of one studio a month holds, the company breaks even in Month 5 and cash never falls below 7,640, which would make it default alive.

scenarios.change: Half the base pace: 5 studios by Month 11.
Two new studios a month: 20 by Month 11.

funding_reason: The pessimistic case never drops below 7,280, well above a buffer of six months of costs (900). No raise is needed for this plan.

reconciliation.check: Ending cash equals starting cash plus net income
Annual summary equals the sum of the months
reconciliation.result: Revenue 2,600 and costs 1,800 match the monthly table.
The business plan shows 4,800 for the first year, which assumes ten studios for all twelve months. This model adds one studio a month, so the first year gives 2,600.

assumptions.text: One new studio a month from Month 2, reaching 10 in Month 11, from the business plan's ten-studio objective.
No studio cancels in the model period. Unit economics use 3% monthly churn instead.
Scenarios: half pace gives 30 studio-months and 1,200 revenue; double pace gives 130 studio-months and 5,200 revenue. Costs stay at 1,800.
